<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const), valueSchemaFor (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const), valueSchemaFor (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5b2dbcc768333bcc62c672144fcf0feb694495ca` — the merge of head `70dd701ebef21d4308a049722739980ab66f8d23` into base `33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5b2dbcc768333bcc62c672144fcf0feb694495ca && git checkout 5b2dbcc768333bcc62c672144fcf0feb694495ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f 70dd701ebef21d4308a049722739980ab66f8d23 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f && git merge --no-ff 70dd701ebef21d4308a049722739980ab66f8d23

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33ee9aa1a0f5273ea9f4d51bfface58d3885ec4f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0d181d4145a22f1170df2328feb87b77922f8d23`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-reference-name-visible.ts (`servableNameField`, `serveReferenceNames`), packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts (`resolveDisplayField`, `resolveRecordDisplayName`, `isTitleEligible`), docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md (D4–D6), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-reference-name-visible.test.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json + packages/spec/scripts/lib/dropped-refinements.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, .changeset/29579-reference-name-only-value.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the gate the declaration pair is judged by)

Inputs read: card #29579 body + its 3 comments (triage 6587041711, claim 6588872858, dev report 6589979343); PR #29623 body, 19-file list, net diff against merge base `81cd9eb0e9`; the 42 check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (generated references, api-surface / export-origins / declaration-map / json-schema.manifest shards, strictness-ledger counts, pin-count tests) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; it was read to judge the `hits`, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New public exports `ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema` (const) and `ReferenceNameOnlyValue` (type) from `@objectstack/spec/data`** — api-surface/data.json +2, export-origins +2, declaration-map +2, json-schema.manifest +1. Right: a closed `strictObject` of `id` (`ReferenceIdValueSchema`), `name` (`z.string().min(1)`), `readRefused` (`z.literal(true)`), built exactly as the `FileRefusedValueSchema` precedent (same helper, same `surface`/`history` wiring, same read-only docblock). The isomorphic pin (818 → 819) is right: no default, no transform, `z.input` equals `z.infer`.
- **`valueSchemaFor(def, 'expanded')` for the reference types becomes `z.union([ReferenceIdValueSchema, ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema, z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())])`.** Accept set unchanged — right. The open `z.record` member already accepted every object the strict member accepts; the strict member precedes it, and a zod 4 union answers with the first member that parses, so `{ id, name, readRefused: true }` now parses through member 2 with byte-identical output (no transform on either side). An expanded record that happens to carry exactly `id`, `name`, `readRefused: true` (a narrow `$select` on a target with such a column) takes member 2 instead of member 3 — same output, same verdict. A wider object (`{ id, name, readRefused: true, owner }`) fails the strict member on `unrecognized_keys` and falls through to `z.record` — same verdict as before (the new test pins the strict schema alone refusing it, and `ok(...)` through the union is not asserted for that case, which is fine). A non-string `id` (`{ id: 42, ... }`) falls through to `z.record` — same verdict. The only observable change is on inputs that already failed (a number, a boolean on an expanded lookup): the `invalid_union` issue now carries three branch issue sets instead of two. Error detail, not a verdict. `multiple: true` wraps the same element union in `z.array`, so the per-element claim holds.
- **The stored form stays `ReferenceIdValueSchema` alone** — right, and pinned by `bad({ type: 'lookup' }, { id, name, readRefused: true })`.
- **`referenceNameVisible` describe + JSDoc** (`field.zod.ts` ~L1733–1782): names the ADR-0079 D4 order (`nameField`, else `displayNameField`, else derived title) and `resolveRecordDisplayName`; names `ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema`; lists five `Record #` floor cases plus the missing/empty-name floor. Judged right against `servableNameField` and the resolver — see ④.
- **objectql `engine-reference-name-visible.ts`**: the hand-written `interface ReferenceNameOnlyValue` goes; the type is `import type`d from `@objectstack/spec/data`, which the module already imports at run time. Type-only, erased; the module is not re-exported from the objectql entry (grep: `engine.ts` imports `serveReferenceNames` only). No published objectql surface moves. Right.
- **authorable-surface/data.json +3 rows** (`data/ReferenceNameOnlyValue:id`, `:name`, `:readRefused`): the mechanical reachability walk over exported object schemas, exactly as `data/FileRefusedValue:id` / `:metadataRefused` already sit in the same shard. Right as a measurement; what it entails for the declaration pair is ②.
- **dropped-refinements.baseline.json +1 row** (`data/ReferenceNameOnlyValue`, site `id`): right. `ReferenceIdValueSchema`'s `.refine` (the embedded-record text guard) is a `custom` check with no JSON-schema projection; nested under the new export it is observed at path `id`, mirroring the existing `data/ReferenceIdValue` row at site `''`. The ledger is hand-edited by design ("a new gap has to be a reviewed line in a diff") — this is that reviewed line. Consequence worth stating: the published JSON schema for `ReferenceNameOnlyValue.id` is wider than the runtime (it does not refuse `{`/`[`-prefixed text), the same gap `ReferenceIdValue` already carries.
- **Generated references** (`field-value.mdx` gains the section; `field.mdx`, `object.mdx`, `system/migration.mdx` carry the new describe; index count 1604 → 1605): consistent with the source; `check:generated` all 14 current per the dev; `Spec property liveness` check-run success.

### ② Semver level

**Wrong as declared, and the gate says so: `Check Changeset` on this head concluded `failure` — annotation "metadata-protocol `added` contradicts clause-② `no`" (verdict `contradiction`, reason `added-under-no`).** That check-run conclusion is the gate verdict and is read as such.

What the gate requires on THIS diff, read from `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`:

- The diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` (+3 rows). That path is in `PROTOCOL_BASELINE_ROOTS`, so a declared `Metadata-protocol: none` is refused (`none-baseline-moved`: "`none` declared while the diff moves an `authorable-surface/` … shard — a protocol change the ratchet can see → exit 1"). Option B of the dev's open question (`none` + spec `patch`) is therefore not available: it trades one red for another.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` beside `Clause-②: no` is refused (`contradiction`). The gate's own remedy text: "`Clause-②: yes` (plus `(widening)` if you like) beside `added`, or a kind that is not `added` beside `no`" — and `narrowed`/`semantic` are false here.
- So the only pair this diff can carry is **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` + `Metadata-protocol: added`**, with `@objectstack/spec: minor` (which the changeset already has).

That pair is also the honest one, not merely the one that greens. The dev measured `Clause-②` on the accept-set half only ("z.record already accepted the value") and that half is correctly `no`. But the line asks two things — 「本卡放宽接受集**或扩大公开面**吗」 (does the card widen the accept set OR enlarge the public surface) — and this diff enlarges the public surface by two exports (api-surface/data.json +2). The precedent is on file: the `FileRefusedValueSchema` entry (`02d9f69`, spec CHANGELOG) declared `Clause-②: yes` for exactly this move — a served-only read form given a named export and joined into the expanded union.

- Changeset `.changeset/29579-reference-name-only-value.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor` — right for `added`. Body prose is accurate (read form only; open member already accepted the value; which name; when withheld). Its `Clause-②: no` line must change with the PR body's: AGENTS.md puts both declarations in both carriers, and the gate re-reads the PR body on `edited` but the changeset only on push.
- No objectql changeset: accepted. The objectql hunk is a type-only import in a module no entry point re-exports; objectql is a tsup-bundled package, so the emitted `dist/` carries no new byte (the dev's 0-hit / 1-hit positive-control measurement is consistent with the gate's own note that a bundled module nothing reaches contributes no emitted byte). The gate grades a moved package with no entry as neither offender nor raised, so with the pair corrected its verdict is `discharged` (spec `minor` raised, objectql ungraded). Not the "bug fix in a released package" case that AGENTS.md says must take `patch`.
- `Clause-②:` line, corrected: `yes (widening)`. `Metadata-protocol: added`. Level `minor` on spec. ADR-0087 disposition: not owed (no narrowing arm, nothing breaking).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question (keep `added` vs `none`)**: answered above — **A, keep `added`**, and the gate additionally requires `Clause-②: yes (widening)` beside it. `none` is refused by `none-baseline-moved`; the AGENTS.md sentence "what a metadata author can write" is read by the gate through the authorable-surface ratchet, and that ratchet counts every exported object schema's keys, served-only forms included (`FileRefusedValue` rows sit beside the new ones). The triage's own reading agrees: "declaring the served shape on the contract is a protocol addition, so p1".
- **Dev flag — `engine.ts` private `serveReferenceNames` docblock (~L13860) names one floor case of five**: confirmed on `main` (`engine.ts:13863`). Private, not emitted, outside this card's file surface and outside `hits`. Escalated as a carrier-none note for the server lane; not a finding on this PR.
- **Dev deviation — dropped-refinements row added "because the build refused without it"**: that is the ratchet working as designed (a new dropped site must be a reviewed line); judged right in ①.
- **Dev deviation — Clause-② measured `no`**: wrong by the gate and by the line's second clause; must-fix in ④.
- **Names needing maintainer approval before merge** (triage 6587041711, claim 6588872858): `ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema` / `ReferenceNameOnlyValue` / `readRefused` as a declared key. Not a reviewer's call; escalated to the maintainer with the summary below. The names are consistent with the sibling precedent (`FileRefusedValueSchema` / `FileRefusedValue` / `metadataRefused`) and with the engine's prior exported interface name, so approval does not reopen the design.
- **Seat freeze** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/identity/protocol.ts` until 06:00 UTC 3 Nov): none of the 19 files touches them. **No engine behaviour change**: confirmed, the objectql hunk is type-only.
- **Check-runs still `in_progress` at review time** (Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Type Check workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint lanes, Live E2E UI, Build Docs): their conclusions are not read as PASS here; this record's verdict rests on `Check Changeset: failure` and on ④, and does not need them.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` — the `referenceNameVisible` describe, against `servableNameField` (objectql, head L213–238) and ADR-0079 D4–D6.** The served value goes to a reader who cannot read the target, so every word of exposure was checked against the code:

- *Which name.* `servableNameField` reads `resolveDisplayField(targetSchema)` = `nameField ?? displayNameField ?? deriveDisplayField(fields)` (display-name.ts:233), and `serveReferenceNames` passes only `{ id, [thatField] }` to `resolveRecordDisplayName` (engine L145–147), which reads the same field. The describe's "its object's `nameField`, else its `displayNameField`, else the derived title field" is exactly D4. Holds.
- *Floor case 1, FLS:* `getReadableFields(referenceObject, caller)` not including the field → `undefined` (L233–234). Describe: "when the reader may not read that field". Holds.
- *Floor case 2, `maskingRule`:* L226. Holds.
- *Floor case 3, formula hop:* `def.type === 'formula' && this.formulaReadsReference(...)` (L227). Describe: "it is a formula reading through another reference". Holds.
- *Floor case 4, explicit pointer at a column neither title-typed nor autonumber:* L225 `!isTitleEligible(def) && def.type !== 'autonumber'`. A derived field is title-eligible by construction (D5), so only an explicit pointer reaches this branch — the describe's word "explicit" is accurate, and `autonumber` as the one non-text explicit primary is D5. A non-text `formula` pointer is caught by the same line and is covered by the same clause. An explicit pointer at a column that does not exist (`def` undefined, L223) also floors; the describe's wording covers it (such a column is neither title-typed nor autonumber) and the closing clause covers it. Holds.
- *Floor case 5, no usable field-level answer:* security not `usable` (L229), no `getReadableFields` (L231), or it throws (L235). Describe: "no field-level answer can be had for the reader". Holds.
- *Missing/empty-name floor:* `resolveDisplayField` undefined → `servableNameField` undefined → `shown = { id }` → `Record #id`; a resolvable field whose value is null/blank → `isEmptyish` → `Record #id` (display-name.ts:262–271, D6). Describe: "A target with no resolvable or no non-empty name reads as the same floor, as it does for every reader." Holds.
- *Exposure bound.* "Nothing else of the target": the engine's name read projects `['id', nameField]` or `['id']` (L127) and the served object is built from `id` and the resolver output only (L147); the schema is closed. Holds. The describe's new sentence "the name field is read only where nothing the security layer owns must be computed" is the module header's own statement (L52–61). Holds.
- *The existing spec pin* (`field-reference-name-visible.test.ts` L172–186) still passes on the new text (`nameField`, `{ id, name, readRefused: true }`, no `#NNNN`, the three bounds) — but it pins none of what this card changed. See should-fix 1.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` — `ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema` against its first consumer (the engine) and the ruling.** `id` is `String(row.id)` of a row the engine itself read (L142, L147), so it is a non-empty string and never `{`/`[`-prefixed — `ReferenceIdValueSchema` holds on every served value. `name` is `resolveRecordDisplayName`'s answer: either a non-empty column value or `Record #id` with `id` set — never empty, so `min(1)` holds. `readRefused` is the literal `true` the engine writes. `bareIdsOf` (L85–90) only collects non-object elements and `valueFor` (L154–158) leaves objects untouched, so a record the caller already expanded is never overwritten by this value — the union's open member and the strict member describe disjoint producers. Tried to break it: a `multiple: true` field mixing a served value and a bare id parses per element (new test pins it); a wider object is refused by the strict schema alone and admitted by the union through the open member (correct: it is an expanded record, not this value). The one latent ambiguity — an expanded target record that genuinely has a `readRefused` column — predates this PR (the marker shipped in #29576) and the key name is the maintainer's to approve; it is not a finding against this schema.

**Findings**

- **Must-fix 1 (FAIL).** The declaration pair contradicts and the `Check Changeset` gate concluded `failure` on this head. Flip `Clause-②: no` → `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in BOTH the PR body and `.changeset/29579-reference-name-only-value.md`; keep `Metadata-protocol: added` and `@objectstack/spec: minor`. Do not take option B (`none`/`patch`): `none-baseline-moved` refuses it because the authorable-surface shard moves. One commit (the changeset) plus the body edit.
- **Should-fix 1.** `packages/spec/src/data/field-reference-name-visible.test.ts` pins the pre-#29579 describe only. Add pins for what this card changed so the describe cannot drift back: `displayNameField`, `ReferenceNameOnlyValueSchema`, and one marker per floor case (e.g. `maskingRule`, `formula reading through another reference`, `neither title-typed nor autonumber`, `no field-level answer`, `no non-empty name`). Test-only; same PR or a follow-up.
- **Should-fix 2.** The JSDoc says "an explicit `nameField` (or `displayNameField`) points at a column …" while the shipped `.describe()` says "an explicit `nameField` points at …". `resolveDisplayField` honours either pointer, so the describe (the text that publishes) should carry the alias too, or say "an explicit title pointer". One clause.
- Noted, no fix owed here: the private `engine.ts` docblock (~L13860) names one floor case of five — server lane, carrier none.

### Closure

- **M1 — declaration pair (closed).** Changeset line `Clause-②: no` → `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: added` and `@objectstack/spec: minor` kept. Each literal was checked against the concatenated `.describe()` string at this head and is a verbatim substring. The header comment's description of the key is updated to match.

The three reference pages that carry the field describe are regenerated with the same sentence; `field-value.mdx` is rightly untouched (its text did not change).

None. The delta is declaration lines, one clause of the shipped describe, test pins and regenerated prose; it introduces no schema, export, accept-set or behaviour change, and nothing in it is false against the code read for the prior record. The prior ① and ④ judgments stand on this head unchanged.
